What exists: 8 new untracked contract/plan/lifecycle JSON files versus 1 new runtime file (scan_conclusion_guard.py) and 4 modified files. The ratio of documentation-to-code is ~8:1. The "implementation queue" exists only as a contract document (redcap-continuous-revival-plan.json), not as executable code. This is a plan about planning, not implementation.
main_concern: Contract proliferation without implementation: 8 untracked JSON contract/lifecycle/Prism-request files have been generated but the only new runtime code is scan_conclusion_guard.py — which itself has no tests. The revival implementation queue and formal usability checker that this Prism review was asked to evaluate do not exist in any executable form. top_risks: Closeout-recursion loop: 4 separate Prism request JSON files exist (revival-implementation-plan, scan-conclusion-guard, scan-conclusion-guard-noise, pre-execution-discussion-intent) for what is fundamentally one task — each review spawns more contracts, each contract spawns more reviews, never reaching executable implementation.

Untested guard claiming completion: scan_conclusion_guard.py is new and untested, yet evidence item #3 claims 'scan_complete=true and conclusion scope allows final scan conclusions' — an untested guard confirming its own scope is a self-referential verification with no ground truth.

minimum_fix: Before another Prism review: (1) implement the revival queue as an actual Python module (e.g., runtime/core/revival_queue.py) with at least one test that verifies it correctly distinguishes done vs. pending items; (2) implement the formal usability checker as code, not a contract document; (3) add a test for scan_conclusion_guard.py that verifies it rejects an intentionally incomplete scan. Do not generate additional contract/lifecycle/Prism-request JSON files until these three implementation artifacts exist.
